During a recent programming contest, I submitted a solution to a dynamic programming problem that passed the sample tests but failed on hidden test cases. The error message I received was simply "Wrong Answer on Test Case 7" without any further details.

This vague feedback made it hard to identify the root cause. I spent nearly 30 minutes manually debugging, adding print statements, and trying to guess the structure of the failing input. Eventually, I discovered that I had misunderstood a constraint mentioned briefly in the problem description â€” something the error message didnâ€™t hint at.

Because of this, I lost valuable time and wasn't able to complete an easier problem I could have solved. If the error message had provided more context (like the input for the failing case or expected vs. actual output), I could have corrected the issue much faster.

1. Quick Debugging Help

AI can quickly identify off-by-one errors, logic bugs, or edge cases based on the code and problem description. This can save precious minutes during a contest.

Example: If your solution fails a hidden test case, an AICA could suggest likely input patterns that might be causing the failure (e.g., maximum constraints, all-zero inputs, etc.).

2. Clarifying Problem Statements

Sometimes, problem descriptions are vague or complex. An AICA could help rephrase or summarize the statement, highlight key constraints, or identify potential edge cases.

Helpful for: Avoiding misinterpretation and saving time on rereading.

3. Generating Test Cases

AI can assist in generating custom test cases, especially edge cases or large inputs, to validate your solution before submitting.

4. Time-Saving Snippets

AI could offer boilerplate code or quick template suggestions (e.g., for Dijkstraâ€™s algorithm, segment trees, or DFS), letting you focus on logic rather than setup.

5. Strategy Suggestions

For harder problems, AICAs might suggest potential approach strategies â€” e.g., â€œTry dynamic programming with state (i, j)â€ or â€œThis looks like a greedy + binary search combo.â€

While it wouldn't solve the problem for you (and most contests prohibit that), it could nudge your thinking in the right direction.

6. Post-Contest Learning

After the contest, AICAs are excellent for analyzing editorial solutions, explaining them step-by-step, or even helping you rewrite them in your preferred language.
